answer_1.quote: In this paper, we try to explore the compositional generalization for multi-attribute controllable dialogue generation... We propose a Disentangled Controllable Generation model (DCG), for compositional generalization in multi-attribute controllable dialogue generation.

answer_2.quote: We use the BLEUs and METEOR to measure the match scores between generated responses and ground-truth references. ... For the control of coarse-grained discrete attributes ... we use the classification accuracy, i.e., E-ACC and A-ACC ... For the control of fine-grained continuous attributes ... we calculate the cosine similarity ... and a Roberta-based NLI model ... We also propose a unified model-based evaluation metric, i.e., MAE.

answer_3.quote: Specifically, the evaluation of each attribute is converted to a text-to-text generation task, just like. T5 is used as the base model for our work... We take the probability of generating "yes" corresponding to <mask> token as the controllability score. ... We also implement MAE on another PLM, BART, to demonstrate generality for our model.
methods: prompt-based evaluation where attribute description and response are fed to T5/BART and the probability of "yes" is used as the score

answer_4.quote: We further deploy a set of human evaluations to compare the controllability and text quality between several methods. 5 human annotators are invited to evaluate on a scale of 1-3... For the text quality, we ask the annotators to evaluate the fluency and context relevancy of the generated responses on a scale of 1-5.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rate controllability (emotion, act, persona) on a 1-3 scale and fluency and relevance on a 1-5 scale.
